name: Scopa Bazzica
description: Two-player Scopa variant from Italy in which players capture table cards by matching value or sum, score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, and primiera, plus optional Bazzica (three cards summing to 9 or less) or Bazzicotto (three of a kind) declared after each three-card deal. First to 21 or 31 points wins.

content.text: Two-player Scopa variant from Italy in which players capture table cards by matching value or sum, score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, and primiera, plus optional Bazzica (three cards summing to 9 or less) or Bazzicotto (three of a kind) declared after each three-card deal. First to 21 or 31 points wins.

Scopa is one of Italy's major card games, with roots in Naples and possible links to Spanish games such as Primero. Bazzica is a traditional two-player Scopa variant in which players score extra points by declaring three-card combinations (Bazzica or Bazzicotto) after each deal; it is documented as part of Italian card-game tradition.
Two players only. Scopa Bazzica is designed for head-to-head play with no partnership or team option.
Standard 40-card Italian deck (coins, cups, swords, batons; King 10, Horse/Queen 9, Jack 8, 7-2 face value, Ace 1).

Dealer shuffles; opponent cuts. Deal one card at a time until each player has three cards; place the next four cards face up on the table. If three or four Kings appear in the table layout, redeal. After each round of three cards played, deal three more to each player (no new table cards). Repeat until deck is empty.
